proxy_language: Proto-Afroasiatic (Levantine/Natufian-adjacent; Semitic-biased reconstruction notation) with a secondary Proto-Semitic surface layer
proxy_rationale: PPNA (c. 9500-8700 BCE; Jericho, Gobekli Tepe, Mureybet, Nemrik, Jerf el-Ahmar) has no attested language. Archaeologists often link the Natufian-PPNA Levant to an Afroasiatic homeland hypothesis (Ehret; Militarev), though Proto-Afroasiatic is itself disputed and dated roughly 10-12 kya or older, and alternatives such as an unknown substrate language, early Proto-Elamo-Dravidian or Hurro-Urartian-like northern layers are possible for Upper Mesopotamia. The most defensible practical proxy for a name builder is a Proto-Afroasiatic/Proto-Semitic-style consonantal-root language. The link to any actual PPNA population is weak and unprovable; all forms are schematic reconstructions.
phonology: Reconstruction-based consonant-heavy inventory (after Ehret 1995, Militarev/Starling, Proto-Semitic as a controlled proxy). Stops: b p t d k g q (glottal stop ', pharyngeal ' and h variants treated as ' and h); emphatics written with dot-free digraphs for ASCII: t' q (ejective/emphatic series). Fricatives: s z sh h kh gh. Sonorants: m n l r w y. Vowels: a i u (short/long, simplified to a i u plus e o only in loan-like cases). Glottal stop and pharyngeals are phonemic. No tone; stress is not written.
phonotactics: Canonical syllables CV, CVC (rarely CVCC word-finally). No initial vowels (initial glottal stop ' is written or the vowel is avoided). No vowel sequences within a root (hiatus broken by ' or y/w). Roots are triconsonantal (C1C2C3) in Semitic proxy, with biconsonantal and monoconsonantal older layers in Afroasiatic; vowels are mostly supplied by the pattern, so words are typically 2-3 syllables. Word-final consonants are freely allowed, no word-final voiced-obstruent devoicing written. Clusters are limited to the root-internal CC across syllable boundary (e.g. -rb-, -nk-, -sm-); initial clusters avoided.
orthography: Scholarly-style Latin transliteration, ASCII-friendly: ' for glottal stop/pharyngeal, kh, gh, sh digraphs, q for the emphatic velar/uvular, vowels a i u (long vowels may be doubled, e.g. aa ii uu, or given a macron). Reconstructed forms would take an asterisk but game names are written without it. No capital-letter distinctions beyond sentence/name capitalization.
morphology: Root-and-pattern (templatic) morphology in the Semitic proxy: a triconsonantal root fits vocalic patterns (a-a, a-i, u-u, etc.) to make nouns and verbs. Nominal affixes: masculine unmarked, feminine -t (-at), plural -uu/-iin or -aat, dual -aan/-ayn (proxy). Prefix ma- for place/instrument nouns (ma-C1C2C3, e.g. maskan 'dwelling', maqtal 'place of killing'), prefix ta- for abstracts/nomina actionis, prefix mu- for agent participles, suffix -aan/-uun for collectives. Definiteness is not marked (no article in Proto-Semitic). Reduplication is used for intensives, plurals of colors/qualities, and onomatopoeic words (e.g. CVCCVC from CVC).
compounding: Genitive construct (idafa-style): head noun first, then modifying noun, with an optional genitive linker -i (proxy) or simply juxtaposition: bayt-i X 'house of X'. 'X-maker' formed with mu- participle + noun or ba'al ('master/owner of') + noun: ba'al-X. Place names: ma- prefix + root or bayt/qiryat 'house/settlement' + noun. Adjectives follow the noun and agree in gender and number. No productive noun-noun compound like Germanic; instead use construct chains or ma-/ba'al- derivations.
noun_phrase_order: Head noun, then genitive/possessor, then adjective(s), then demonstrative. Possessive suffixes attach to the head noun. Numerals precede or follow depending on proxy; default to follow the noun.

notes: All forms are schematic reconstructions; actual PPNA languages are unknown and may not be Afroasiatic at all. The forbidden_patterns include a naive check against stray glottal stops at word start and against e/o/f/v/j/x/c; the last initial-glottal pattern is intentionally conservative and may need loosening if names begin with '. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word unless the language is Goidelic; Afroasiatic-style forms like these will not collide. Confidence is speculative: use for flavor, not as a claim about PPNA speech.
